ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a large outer triangle, and inside it there is a larger inner triangle formed by connecting the midpoints of the three sides of the outer triangle; this inner triangle as a whole is shaded gray. Inside the gray inner triangle, smaller triangles constructed by midpoints continue to appear, and at the innermost part a small white unshaded triangular hole is visible. Reasoning: The vertices of each inscribed triangle are all on the midpoints of the three sides of the circumscribed triangle, so it is a medial triangle; the side length is reduced to 1/2 of the original, and the area is reduced to 1/4 of the original. The area of the largest triangle is 64, so the area of the first-level inscribed triangle is 64/4 = 16. The small white hole in the figure is the third-level inscribed triangle relative to the largest triangle, so its area is 64/4^3 = 1. The shaded part equals the area of the first-level gray inner triangle minus this small white hole area, namely 16 - 1 = 15.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large outer triangle with a shaded first inscribed medial triangle, and with a small unshaded triangular hole inside the nested midpoint construction. From the text, each inscribed triangle is formed by joining midpoints, so each new triangle has area one fourth of its circumscribed triangle. Starting from area 64, the first inscribed triangle has area 64/4 = 16. The visible small white hole is two more midpoint-inscription steps inside that first triangle, so its area is 64/4^3 = 1. The shaded region is the first inscribed triangle minus this small unshaded hole: 16 - 1 = 15.

method.method_draft: Use a complement count. From the diagram, the shaded part lies inside the largest triangle; the unshaded parts consist of the three corner triangles outside the first medial triangle plus the small central white triangle. By the midpoint rule, the first medial construction divides the largest triangle into four equal-area triangles, so the three outside corner triangles have total area 3(64/4) = 48. The small central white triangle is obtained after three successive midpoint-area reductions from the largest triangle, so its area is 64/4^3 = 1. Therefore the shaded area is the whole outer area minus all unshaded pieces: 64 - 48 - 1 = 15.
